claims.text: The starting monolithic CoCrFeNi alloy has a homogeneous FCC microstructure.
In situ processing can form TiC and Al2O3 ceramic phases within the proposed CoCrFeNi matrix.
The in situ ceramic phases will be uniformly dispersed in the CoCrFeNi matrix.
TiC and/or Al2O3 particles will act as load-bearing reinforcements.
The ceramic particles will provide nucleation sites for protective tribofilms across the test-temperature range.
At low temperatures, the ceramic particles will impede surface deformation.
At low temperatures, the ceramic particles will impede micro-plowing.
Suppressing surface deformation and micro-plowing will reduce friction and wear.
At elevated temperatures up to 800 °C, the ceramic particles will maintain their structural integrity.
At elevated temperatures, the ceramic particles will promote formation of lubricious oxide films.
The lubricious oxide films will continue to reduce friction and wear at elevated temperatures.
The ceramic reinforcement and oxide films will counter the elevated-temperature softening tendency of the base alloy.
The TiC/Al2O3-containing composite will have a lower coefficient of friction than monolithic CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The TiC/Al2O3-containing composite will have a significantly lower wear rate than monolithic CoCrFeNi throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The predicted performance is conditional on the ceramic phases remaining thermally stable and well distributed.
The predicted performance is limited to applied loads within the regime for which the composite is engineered.
